blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: Helios is a project-management workspace for planning work, tracking tasks and sharing progress with your team. A workspace contains projects, members, saved views and billing settings.

blocks.heading: Create a workspace
blocks.text: Sign in at app.helios.example and choose Create workspace. Enter a workspace name, choose the US or EU data region, and invite at least one other owner. The region cannot be changed after the workspace is created.

blocks.heading: Invite your team
blocks.text: Open Settings > Members and choose Invite people. Enter one email address per line, pick the Member role and send the invitations. Members can create projects and edit tasks; Viewers can only read.

blocks.heading: Create your first project
blocks.text: Open Projects and choose New project. Give the project a name, choose List or Timeline, and add the first tasks. Every project has a key such as OPS that prefixes task references like OPS-14.

blocks.heading: Notifications
blocks.text: By default Helios sends an email when someone mentions you, assigns you a task, or comments on a task you follow. Change the frequency under Profile > Notifications. A daily digest is sent at 08:00 in your workspace time zone.

blocks.heading: Next steps
blocks.text: Import an existing backlog from CSV under Projects > Import. The importer accepts title, description, assignee, status and due date. You can also connect Slack from Settings > Integrations so task updates appear in a channel.

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: Helios 2.0 organises work into workspaces, projects and tasks. A workspace owns members, guest access, integrations and billing. Projects can use List, Board or Timeline views without changing the underlying tasks.

blocks.heading: Create a workspace
blocks.text: Sign in at app.helios.example and choose Create workspace. Enter a workspace name, choose the US or EU data region, and invite at least one other owner. The region cannot be changed after the workspace is created.

blocks.heading: Invite your team
blocks.text: Open Settings > Members and choose Invite people. Pick Member, Viewer or Guest before sending. Guests only see projects they are explicitly added to and cannot open billing or admin settings.

blocks.heading: Create your first project
blocks.text: Open Projects and choose New project, or start from a template in the project gallery. Choose List, Board or Timeline. A task can have an assignee, due date, labels, attachments and a priority.

blocks.heading: Invite guests
blocks.text: Guests are external collaborators. Add a guest to a project from the project Members tab. Guests can comment and upload files, but they cannot create projects, invite other people or view the workspace member directory.

blocks.heading: Use a template
blocks.text: Templates copy a project structure, including sections, task titles, checklists and custom fields. Open the project gallery, choose a template and select Use template. Template changes do not affect projects that were created earlier.

blocks.heading: Next steps
blocks.text: Connect Slack or GitHub from Settings > Integrations. Import an existing backlog from CSV under Projects > Import. Workspace owners can also enable SAML SSO from Settings > Security.

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: Helios 3.0 is a project-management workspace with projects, tasks, milestones and workload planning. Press Command-K or Ctrl-K anywhere to open the command palette and jump to a project, task or setting.

blocks.heading: Create a workspace
blocks.text: Sign in at app.helios.example and choose Create workspace. Enter a workspace name, choose the US or EU data region, and invite at least one other owner. The region cannot be changed after the workspace is created.

blocks.heading: Invite your team
blocks.text: Open Settings > Members and choose Invite people. Choose Member, Viewer or Guest. Guests only see the projects they are added to, while Viewers can read every project but cannot edit tasks or settings.

blocks.heading: Create your first project
blocks.text: Create a project from Projects > New project or from a workspace template. Choose List, Board, Timeline or Workload. Add tasks with an owner, due date, estimate, labels and dependencies.

blocks.heading: Use the command palette
blocks.text: Press Command-K on macOS or Ctrl-K on Windows and Linux. Type a project name, task reference or setting. The palette also runs actions such as Create task, Assign to me and Toggle sidebar.

blocks.heading: Plan with milestones
blocks.text: Milestones group tasks around a delivery date. Open a project, choose Milestones and add a target date. The timeline shows the milestone marker and warns when incomplete tasks fall after it.

blocks.heading: Next steps
blocks.text: Invite your team, connect an integration and review the workspace audit log. Owners can enable SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning from Settings > Security.

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: Projects contain tasks, and tasks can contain subtasks. Use projects for a team initiative and tasks for the individual units of work. Every task has a reference, status, assignee and optional due date.

blocks.heading: Projects and views
blocks.text: List view is the default. Timeline view places tasks on a calendar using start and due dates. Board view groups tasks by status. You can switch views without moving or copying any data.

blocks.heading: Task fields
blocks.text: A task stores a title, description, assignee, reporter, status, priority, due date and labels. Subtasks inherit the project but keep their own assignee and status.

blocks.heading: Status and workflow
blocks.text: The default workflow is Backlog, To do, In progress and Done. Admins can rename statuses and choose which status counts as closed. Moving a task to a closed status records the completion date.

blocks.heading: Comments and mentions
blocks.text: Comments support @mentions and file attachments. Mentioned members receive a notification even if they do not follow the task. Edit history is available from the task menu.

blocks.heading: Saved views and export
blocks.text: Filters can be saved as a personal or shared view. Export the current view to CSV from the view menu; exports include visible columns only.

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: Projects contain tasks, subtasks and dependencies. Use dependencies when one task must finish before another can start. Every task has a reference, status, assignee, estimate and optional due date.

blocks.heading: Projects and views
blocks.text: List, Board and Timeline views share the same task data. Timeline draws dependency arrows and highlights tasks that would move a downstream due date. Board view groups tasks by status or assignee.

blocks.heading: Task fields
blocks.text: Task fields include title, description, assignee, reporter, status, priority, estimate, start date, due date, labels and attachments. Custom fields can be added to a project by an Admin.

blocks.heading: Status and workflow
blocks.text: The default workflow is Backlog, To do, In progress, In review and Done. Admins can rename statuses, reorder them and choose which statuses count as closed. A task can move backwards if the workflow allows it.

blocks.heading: Comments and mentions
blocks.text: Comments support @mentions, reactions and file attachments. Editing a comment adds an edited marker and keeps the previous version in the task activity log for 30 days.

blocks.heading: Dependencies and recurring tasks
blocks.text: Open a task, choose Dependencies and add a blocking task. Helios warns when a due date conflicts with an upstream dependency, but it does not block the save. Recurring tasks repeat daily, weekly or monthly and create the next occurrence when the current task is marked Done.

blocks.heading: Saved views and export
blocks.text: Saved views can be personal or shared with the project. A view stores filters, sort order, grouping and visible columns. Exports to CSV include the rows and columns currently visible.

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: Projects contain tasks, subtasks, dependencies and milestones. Use milestones for delivery dates, dependencies for sequencing and workload for capacity planning. Every task has a reference, status, assignee, estimate and optional due date.

blocks.heading: Projects and views
blocks.text: List, Board, Timeline and Workload views share the same task data. Timeline shows dependencies and milestones. Workload groups open task estimates by assignee and week so you can spot overallocation.

blocks.heading: Task fields
blocks.text: Task fields include title, description, assignee, reporter, status, priority, estimate, start date, due date, labels, custom fields and attachments. Estimates use person-days and accept increments of 0.5.

blocks.heading: Status and workflow
blocks.text: The default workflow is Backlog, To do, In progress, In review, Blocked and Done. Admins can rename, reorder and add statuses, and choose which statuses count as closed. A task can move backwards if the workflow allows it.

blocks.heading: Comments and mentions
blocks.text: Comments support @mentions, reactions, file attachments and threaded replies. Editing a comment keeps the previous version in the task activity log for 90 days. Resolving a thread hides it from the default comment view.

blocks.heading: Milestones and workload
blocks.text: Add a milestone from the project sidebar and set a target date. Workload view counts open task estimates per assignee. A person is overallocated when assigned estimates exceed their weekly capacity, which defaults to five person-days.

blocks.heading: Saved views and export
blocks.text: Saved views can be personal, shared with a project or published to the workspace. A view stores filters, sort order, grouping, visible columns and the selected layout. CSV exports include visible rows and columns.

blocks.heading: Automations
blocks.text: Project automations can assign a task, change status or post a comment when a trigger fires. Triggers include task created, status changed and due date approaching. Automations run as the workspace owner and appear in the audit log.

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: API keys authenticate server-to-server requests to the Helios API. Send the key in the Authorization header as a Bearer token. Keys are workspace credentials; never ship them in browser code or mobile apps.

blocks.heading: Create a key
blocks.text: Open Settings > Developer > API keys and choose Create key. The full key is shown once. Copy it before closing the dialog; Helios stores only a fingerprint and cannot show the secret again. Keys inherit the permissions of the member who created them.

blocks.heading: Key lifetime
blocks.text: API keys do not expire. Helios does not provide key rotation in v1. To replace a key, create a second key, deploy it, and then revoke the first key. A workspace can have up to ten active keys.

blocks.heading: Rotate a key
blocks.text: Helios does not provide a rotation action in v1. Create a second key, deploy it, verify traffic, and then revoke the first key. A workspace can have up to ten active keys.

blocks.heading: Scopes
blocks.text: Keys have workspace-wide access in v1. There are no read-only or project-scoped keys. Create a separate key per service so that one credential can be revoked without interrupting other integrations.

blocks.heading: Revoke a key
blocks.text: Key creation and revocation appear in Settings > Audit log. Requests made with a key are attributed to the key owner in project activity.

blocks.heading: Common errors
blocks.text: 401 invalid_key means the key is unknown or malformed. 401 key_expired means the key passed its 90-day limit. 403 insufficient_scope means the key is valid but lacks the scope required by the endpoint. Include the request ID from the response when contacting support.

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: API keys authenticate server-to-server requests to the Helios API. Send the key in the Authorization header as a Bearer token. Keys are workspace credentials; never ship them in browser code or mobile apps.

blocks.heading: Create a key
blocks.text: Open Settings > Developer > API keys and choose Create key. Choose the read, write or admin scope, name the key and copy the secret from the confirmation dialog. The full key is shown once; Helios stores only a fingerprint.

blocks.heading: Key lifetime
blocks.text: API keys expire 90 days after creation. The API returns HTTP 401 with the error code key_expired for an expired key. Rotate keys before day 90; in v2 the old key stops working as soon as rotation completes.

blocks.heading: Rotate a key
blocks.text: Open Settings > Developer > API keys, select a key and choose Rotate. The replacement key is shown once and keeps the same scopes. Update the service environment variable before the old key is revoked; the old key stops working when rotation completes.

blocks.heading: Scopes
blocks.text: Choose scopes when creating a key: read, write or admin. Read keys can list projects and tasks; write keys can create and update them; admin keys can also manage members and webhooks. Grant the smallest scope that the integration needs.

blocks.heading: Revoke a key
blocks.text: Key creation, rotation and revocation emit audit events with the actor, key prefix and source IP address. Request logs retain the key prefix, never the secret.

blocks.heading: Common errors
blocks.text: 401 invalid_key means the key is unknown or malformed. 401 key_expired means the key passed its 90-day limit. 403 insufficient_scope means the key is valid but lacks the scope required by the endpoint. Include the request ID from the response when contacting support.

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: API keys authenticate server-to-server requests to the Helios API. Send the key in the Authorization header as a Bearer token. Keys are workspace credentials; never ship them in browser code or mobile apps.

blocks.heading: Create a key
blocks.text: Open Settings > Developer > API keys and choose Create key. Choose the read, write or admin scope, optionally limit the key to specific projects on a Business plan, name the key and copy the secret from the confirmation dialog. The full key is shown once.

blocks.heading: Key lifetime
blocks.text: API keys expire 90 days after creation. Rotation creates a 24-hour overlap: the replacement key works immediately and the old key keeps working until the overlap ends. After 24 hours the old key returns HTTP 401 with the error code key_expired.

blocks.heading: Rotate a key
blocks.text: Open Settings > Developer > API keys, select a key and choose Rotate. Choose the overlap window (1 to 24 hours, default 24) and copy the new key. The replacement inherits the original scopes unless you edit them before confirming.

blocks.heading: Scopes
blocks.text: Choose scopes when creating a key: read, write, admin or a comma-separated combination such as read,write. Admin keys can manage members, webhooks and billing exports. Project-scoped keys are available on Business plans and restrict access to listed projects.

blocks.heading: Revoke a key
blocks.text: Key creation, rotation, scope changes and revocation emit audit events with the actor, key prefix and source IP address. The audit log retains key events for 365 days. Request logs retain the key prefix, never the secret.

blocks.heading: Common errors
blocks.text: 401 invalid_key means the key is unknown or malformed. 401 key_expired means the key passed its 90-day limit. 403 insufficient_scope means the key is valid but lacks the scope required by the endpoint. Include the request ID from the response when contacting support.

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: Helios has four built-in roles. Owners manage billing, security and the workspace. Admins manage members, projects and integrations. Members create and edit work. Viewers can read projects but cannot change tasks or settings.

blocks.heading: Assign a role
blocks.text: Open Settings > Members, choose a member and select Change role. Every workspace must keep at least one Owner. A member can hold only one built-in role at a time; custom roles are not available in v1.

blocks.heading: Permissions
blocks.text: Only Owners can change the billing plan, delete the workspace or enable SAML. Admins can invite members, create projects and manage webhooks. Members cannot change workspace settings. Viewers cannot comment on tasks or upload attachments.

blocks.heading: Audit log access
blocks.text: The audit log records member invitations, role changes and project deletions. Owners can view the log under Settings > Audit log. Export is not available in v1.

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: Helios has four built-in roles and optional custom roles. Owners manage billing, security and the workspace. Admins manage members, projects and integrations. Members create and edit work. Viewers and Guests have read-only access with different visibility rules.

blocks.heading: Assign a role
blocks.text: Open Settings > Members, choose a member and select Change role. Every workspace must keep at least one Owner. Guests are invited from a project rather than the workspace directory and only see projects they are added to.

blocks.heading: Permissions
blocks.text: Custom roles start from a built-in role and add granular permissions such as project.create, member.invite and audit.export. A custom role cannot grant billing.manage or workspace.delete; those stay with the Owner role. Permission changes apply at the next request.

blocks.heading: Audit log access
blocks.text: Audit log export requires the Owner role or a custom role with the audit.export permission. The export covers the previous 30 days, is delivered as a CSV download, and the download link expires after seven days. Invitations, role changes, project deletions and SSO changes are always recorded.

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: Helios has four built-in roles, optional custom roles and SCIM group mapping. Owners manage billing, security and the workspace. Admins manage members, projects and integrations. Members create and edit work. Viewers and Guests have read-only access with different visibility rules.

blocks.heading: Assign a role
blocks.text: Open Settings > Members, choose a member and select Change role. Every workspace must keep at least one Owner. Guests are invited from a project and only see projects they are added to. With SCIM enabled, group membership can assign built-in roles automatically.

blocks.heading: Permissions
blocks.text: Custom roles start from a built-in role and add granular permissions such as project.create, member.invite, audit.export and webhook.manage. A custom role cannot grant billing.manage or workspace.delete; those stay with the Owner role. Permission changes apply at the next request.

blocks.heading: Audit log access
blocks.text: Audit log export requires the Owner role or a custom role with the audit.export permission. The export covers the previous 90 days, is delivered as a CSV download, and the download link expires after 24 hours. SCIM provisioning events include the source identity provider and the mapped group.

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: Helios bills per active member. Starter is free for up to five members, Team is USD 12 per member per month billed annually, and Business is USD 24 per member per month billed annually. Monthly billing costs 20 percent more.

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: Starter includes three projects and 1 GB of storage. Team includes unlimited projects, 100 GB and standard support. Business includes 500 GB, SAML SSO and a 99.9 percent uptime target.

blocks.heading: Seats and billing cycle
blocks.text: A seat is an active member or guest. Viewers consume a seat. The billing cycle starts on the day the workspace is created and renews on the same day each month or year. Adding a seat mid-cycle is prorated; removing a seat takes effect at the next renewal.

blocks.heading: Invoices and payment
blocks.text: Owners can download invoices from Settings > Billing. Card payments are charged automatically. Annual Business plans can request NET 30 terms during the sales process. Failed payments retry after three and seven days.

blocks.heading: Cancellation and refunds
blocks.text: Cancelling ends the plan at the end of the current term. The workspace becomes read-only for 30 days and is then deleted. Monthly plans are not refunded. Annual plans may receive a refund for unused full months if cancelled within 14 days of purchase.

blocks.heading: Cancellation and refunds
blocks.text: Prices exclude taxes. Helios adds VAT, GST or sales tax when the billing address requires it.

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: Single sign-on lets members authenticate through your identity provider instead of a Helios password. SSO is configured per workspace and can be enforced for every member except the break-glass Owner account.

blocks.heading: Session policy
blocks.text: SAML 2.0 single sign-on is available on the Business plan. Helios supports service-provider-initiated and identity-provider-initiated sign-in. Just-in-time provisioning creates a Member account on first sign-in. SAML sessions expire after 24 hours in v1.

blocks.heading: Provisioning
blocks.text: SCIM provisioning is not supported in v1. Member accounts are created by JIT.

blocks.heading: Configure SAML
blocks.text: In your identity provider, create a SAML application and use the workspace metadata URL from Settings > Security > SSO. Set the ACS URL to https://app.helios.example/saml/acs and the entity ID to the workspace ID shown on the same page.

blocks.heading: Configure SAML
blocks.text: Upload the identity provider metadata XML or enter the SSO URL and signing certificate manually. Helios validates the audience, recipient and signature on every assertion. Clock skew is limited to two minutes.

blocks.heading: Verify domains
blocks.text: Add every email domain that should use SSO and verify it with a DNS TXT record. A domain can belong to only one workspace. Members with an unverified domain continue to sign in with their Helios password unless enforcement is on.

blocks.heading: Enforce SSO
blocks.text: Owners can choose Optional or Required. Required SSO blocks password sign-in for every member whose email domain is verified, except the break-glass Owner. Keep at least two Owners with working SSO access before enabling enforcement.

blocks.heading: Troubleshooting
blocks.text: A signature error usually means the certificate in Helios is stale. An audience mismatch means the entity ID in the identity provider does not match the workspace. After changing certificates, sign out and retry in a private browser window.

blocks.heading: Helios 1.0
blocks.text: Helios 1.0 was released on 2024-01-15. This release introduced workspaces, projects, tasks, List and Timeline views, comments and CSV import. It is the first generally available version of the product.

blocks.heading: Highlights
blocks.text: Projects and tasks with references, statuses, assignees and due dates. Email notifications with an optional daily digest. A workspace member directory with Owner, Admin, Member and Viewer roles.

blocks.heading: Improvements
blocks.text: CSV import now accepts priority and labels. Timeline view remembers the last zoom level. Mention notifications include the comment text instead of only a link.

blocks.heading: Known issues
blocks.text: Timeline drag-and-drop can skip a day when the browser zoom is below 80 percent. CSV import rejects files larger than 10 MB. Viewer accounts can still download attachments if they have the direct link.

blocks.heading: Upgrade notes
blocks.text: No action is required for hosted workspaces. API clients should continue using the v1 endpoints. The legacy /projects.json shape is deprecated but still available until 2024-12-31.

blocks.heading: Helios 2.0
blocks.text: Helios 2.0 was released on 2025-01-15. This release added task dependencies, recurring tasks, guest access, board view and scoped API keys. It also introduced the 2.0 API namespace.

blocks.heading: Highlights
blocks.text: Dependencies with timeline warnings. Recurring tasks for daily, weekly and monthly work. Guests who only see the projects they are added to. API keys with read, write and admin scopes.

blocks.heading: Improvements
blocks.text: Project templates copy sections, checklists and custom fields. Saved views can be shared with a project. Audit events now include the source IP address for key changes.

blocks.heading: Breaking changes
blocks.text: API keys created before 2025-01-15 had no scopes and now behave as admin keys. The legacy Slack command /helios has been replaced by the Slack app. Webhook signatures use SHA-256; SHA-1 signatures are still accepted until 2025-06-30.

blocks.heading: Known issues
blocks.text: The CSV importer does not preserve dependency links. Workload view is not available in 2.0. A recurring task may create two occurrences if the browser retries a failed completion request.

blocks.heading: Helios 3.0
blocks.text: Helios 3.0 was released on 2026-01-15. This release added milestones, workload planning, the command palette, SCIM provisioning and 90-day audit log exports. It also made webhook signature verification mandatory.

blocks.heading: Highlights
blocks.text: Milestones with timeline markers. Workload view for capacity planning. Command palette for navigation and common actions. SAML session policy reduced to 8 hours and SCIM group-to-role mapping.

blocks.heading: Improvements

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: Webhooks send an HTTP POST to your endpoint when an event happens in Helios. Create an endpoint under Settings > Developer > Webhooks, choose the events and store the signing secret securely.

blocks.heading: Signature verification
blocks.text: Each delivery includes an X-Helios-Signature header containing an HMAC-SHA1 digest of the raw request body. Compute the digest with the endpoint secret and compare it in constant time before parsing JSON.

blocks.heading: Retries and delivery
blocks.text: Helios retries failed deliveries three times with a five-minute backoff. A delivery is successful when the endpoint returns any 2xx status within ten seconds. After the final retry the delivery is marked failed and is not retried again.

blocks.heading: Event types
blocks.text: Available events are project.created, project.deleted, task.created, task.updated and task.deleted. Payloads include the workspace ID, event type, timestamp and the changed object.

blocks.heading: Manage endpoints
blocks.text: Rotate a secret from the endpoint menu; the previous secret remains valid for 24 hours. Disable an endpoint to stop new deliveries without deleting its history. Delivery logs retain request headers, response status and latency for 30 days.

blocks.heading: Replay a delivery
blocks.text: Open the endpoint delivery log, select a failed delivery and choose Replay. Replays use the current endpoint secret and count toward the retry budget. A delivery can be replayed up to ten times in 24 hours.

blocks.heading: Slack and Teams
blocks.text: The Slack integration posts task and project updates to a channel and lets members create tasks with the /helios slash command. Link a channel to a project to keep updates in one place.

blocks.heading: GitHub and GitLab
blocks.text: The GitHub integration links pull requests and commits to tasks when the task reference appears in the title or body. Merging a linked pull request can move the task to Done if the project enables it.

blocks.heading: Calendar and Jira
blocks.text: The Google Calendar integration mirrors task due dates into a read-only Helios calendar. The Jira integration links Helios tasks to Jira issues and syncs status in both directions when the mapping is enabled.

blocks.heading: Permissions and limits

blocks.heading: Troubleshooting
blocks.text: If an integration stops posting, check Settings > Integrations for an expired authorization and reconnect it. Slack rate limits can delay messages during busy periods. GitHub events are delivered once; Helios does not replay missed events.

blocks.heading: Scope
blocks.text: This policy covers hosted Helios workspaces. It does not cover data that a customer exports and stores outside Helios. Retention periods are measured from the deletion event in UTC.

blocks.heading: Retention schedule
blocks.text: Deleted projects enter a recoverable state for 30 days and are then purged within seven days. Deleted tasks are purged with their project. Audit logs are retained for 180 days. API request logs are retained for 30 days.

blocks.heading: Retention schedule
blocks.text: Backups are encrypted at rest and retained for 35 days. A backup may contain data that was deleted after the backup was taken; restores are performed only for workspace-level recovery.

blocks.heading: Export before deletion
blocks.text: An Owner can export a project before the recoverable period ends. Exports include tasks, comments, attachments and custom fields. The download link expires after 24 hours and is not included in backups.

blocks.heading: Legal hold
blocks.text: A legal hold suspends deletion for named projects or members until an Owner removes the hold. Legal hold is available on Business plans. Helios notifies the workspace owner before a held project is purged.

blocks.heading: On-premises installation retired
blocks.text: Helios ended sales of the on-premises distribution on 2024-12-31. The final supported on-premises release was 1.8. Helios 2.0 and later are cloud-only, and no installer, license key, activation code or upgrade package is available.

blocks.heading: On-premises installation retired
blocks.text: This page is retained so that old bookmarks and support articles do not return a 404. It does not describe a supported installation procedure for Helios 2.0 or 3.0.

blocks.heading: Why the distribution was retired
blocks.text: Operating a self-hosted deployment required customers to manage PostgreSQL, object storage, search indexes and quarterly security patches. The hosted service now provides the same data residency controls in the US and EU regions.

blocks.heading: Migration to the hosted service
blocks.text: An owner of a 1.x deployment can request a migration assessment from Helios Support. The assessment covers data export, identity provider mapping and a cutover window. Migrations are scheduled by support; there is no self-service migration command.

blocks.heading: Migration to the hosted service
blocks.text: Export the PostgreSQL database and attachment bucket before the assessment. Do not send production credentials by email. Support provides a secure upload link after the request is approved.

blocks.heading: Support boundaries
blocks.text: Support cannot issue installation media, patch an existing 1.x server or provide commands from the retired installer. Security advisories for 1.8 are no longer published. Customers still running 1.x should plan a migration or isolate the server from the public internet.

blocks.heading: Severity levels
blocks.text: SEV-1 is a full workspace outage or confirmed data exposure; page the on-call lead immediately. SEV-2 is a major feature unavailable for more than 30 minutes. SEV-3 is degraded performance with a workaround. Record every incident in the Northwind operations channel.

blocks.heading: Escalation path
blocks.text: Start with the Northwind platform on-call, then the workspace owner, then the Helios support escalation contact. The owner is the only person who can approve a production data restore. During a SEV-1, update the incident channel every 15 minutes until mitigation.

blocks.heading: Maintenance window
blocks.text: Northwind reserves Sunday 02:00–04:00 UTC for changes. No production deploys during quarter-end close or the first two business days of each month. Emergency changes require approval from the workspace owner and the security lead.

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: Helios is a project-management workspace for planning work, tracking tasks and sharing progress with your team. A workspace contains projects, members, saved views and billing settings.

blocks.heading: Create a workspace
blocks.text: Sign in at app.helios.example and choose Create workspace. Enter a workspace name, choose the US or EU data region, and invite at least one other owner. The region cannot be changed after the workspace is created.

blocks.heading: Invite your team
blocks.text: Open Settings > Members and choose Invite people. Enter one email address per line, pick the Member role and send the invitations. Members can create projects and edit tasks; Viewers can only read.

blocks.heading: Create your first project
blocks.text: Open Projects and choose New project. Give the project a name, choose List or Timeline, and add the first tasks. Every project has a key such as OPS that prefixes task references like OPS-14.

blocks.heading: Notifications
blocks.text: By default Helios sends an email when someone mentions you, assigns you a task, or comments on a task you follow. Change the frequency under Profile > Notifications. A daily digest is sent at 08:00 in your workspace time zone.

blocks.heading: Next steps
blocks.text: Import an existing backlog from CSV under Projects > Import. The importer accepts title, description, assignee, status and due date. You can also connect Slack from Settings > Integrations so task updates appear in a channel.

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: Helios 2.0 organises work into workspaces, projects and tasks. A workspace owns members, guest access, integrations and billing. Projects can use List, Board or Timeline views without changing the underlying tasks.

blocks.heading: Create a workspace
blocks.text: Sign in at app.helios.example and choose Create workspace. Enter a workspace name, choose the US or EU data region, and invite at least one other owner. The region cannot be changed after the workspace is created.

blocks.heading: Invite your team
blocks.text: Open Settings > Members and choose Invite people. Pick Member, Viewer or Guest before sending. Guests only see projects they are explicitly added to and cannot open billing or admin settings.

blocks.heading: Create your first project
blocks.text: Open Projects and choose New project, or start from a template in the project gallery. Choose List, Board or Timeline. A task can have an assignee, due date, labels, attachments and a priority.

blocks.heading: Invite guests
blocks.text: Guests are external collaborators. Add a guest to a project from the project Members tab. Guests can comment and upload files, but they cannot create projects, invite other people or view the workspace member directory.

blocks.heading: Use a template
blocks.text: Templates copy a project structure, including sections, task titles, checklists and custom fields. Open the project gallery, choose a template and select Use template. Template changes do not affect projects that were created earlier.

blocks.heading: Next steps
blocks.text: Connect Slack or GitHub from Settings > Integrations. Import an existing backlog from CSV under Projects > Import. Workspace owners can also enable SAML SSO from Settings > Security.

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: Helios 3.0 is a project-management workspace with projects, tasks, milestones and workload planning. Press Command-K or Ctrl-K anywhere to open the command palette and jump to a project, task or setting.

blocks.heading: Create a workspace
blocks.text: Sign in at app.helios.example and choose Create workspace. Enter a workspace name, choose the US or EU data region, and invite at least one other owner. The region cannot be changed after the workspace is created.

blocks.heading: Invite your team
blocks.text: Open Settings > Members and choose Invite people. Choose Member, Viewer or Guest. Guests only see the projects they are added to, while Viewers can read every project but cannot edit tasks or settings.

blocks.heading: Create your first project
blocks.text: Create a project from Projects > New project or from a workspace template. Choose List, Board, Timeline or Workload. Add tasks with an owner, due date, estimate, labels and dependencies.

blocks.heading: Use the command palette
blocks.text: Press Command-K on macOS or Ctrl-K on Windows and Linux. Type a project name, task reference or setting. The palette also runs actions such as Create task, Assign to me and Toggle sidebar.

blocks.heading: Plan with milestones
blocks.text: Milestones group tasks around a delivery date. Open a project, choose Milestones and add a target date. The timeline shows the milestone marker and warns when incomplete tasks fall after it.

blocks.heading: Next steps
blocks.text: Invite your team, connect an integration and review the workspace audit log. Owners can enable SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning from Settings > Security.

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: Projects contain tasks, and tasks can contain subtasks. Use projects for a team initiative and tasks for the individual units of work. Every task has a reference, status, assignee and optional due date.

blocks.heading: Projects and views
blocks.text: List view is the default. Timeline view places tasks on a calendar using start and due dates. Board view groups tasks by status. You can switch views without moving or copying any data.

blocks.heading: Task fields
blocks.text: A task stores a title, description, assignee, reporter, status, priority, due date and labels. Subtasks inherit the project but keep their own assignee and status.

blocks.heading: Status and workflow
blocks.text: The default workflow is Backlog, To do, In progress and Done. Admins can rename statuses and choose which status counts as closed. Moving a task to a closed status records the completion date.

blocks.heading: Comments and mentions
blocks.text: Comments support @mentions and file attachments. Mentioned members receive a notification even if they do not follow the task. Edit history is available from the task menu.

blocks.heading: Saved views and export
blocks.text: Filters can be saved as a personal or shared view. Export the current view to CSV from the view menu; exports include visible columns only.

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: Projects contain tasks, subtasks and dependencies. Use dependencies when one task must finish before another can start. Every task has a reference, status, assignee, estimate and optional due date.

blocks.heading: Projects and views
blocks.text: List, Board and Timeline views share the same task data. Timeline draws dependency arrows and highlights tasks that would move a downstream due date. Board view groups tasks by status or assignee.

blocks.heading: Task fields
blocks.text: Task fields include title, description, assignee, reporter, status, priority, estimate, start date, due date, labels and attachments. Custom fields can be added to a project by an Admin.

blocks.heading: Status and workflow
blocks.text: The default workflow is Backlog, To do, In progress, In review and Done. Admins can rename statuses, reorder them and choose which statuses count as closed. A task can move backwards if the workflow allows it.

blocks.heading: Comments and mentions
blocks.text: Comments support @mentions, reactions and file attachments. Editing a comment adds an edited marker and keeps the previous version in the task activity log for 30 days.

blocks.heading: Dependencies and recurring tasks
blocks.text: Open a task, choose Dependencies and add a blocking task. Helios warns when a due date conflicts with an upstream dependency, but it does not block the save. Recurring tasks repeat daily, weekly or monthly and create the next occurrence when the current task is marked Done.

blocks.heading: Saved views and export
blocks.text: Saved views can be personal or shared with the project. A view stores filters, sort order, grouping and visible columns. Exports to CSV include the rows and columns currently visible.

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: Projects contain tasks, subtasks, dependencies and milestones. Use milestones for delivery dates, dependencies for sequencing and workload for capacity planning. Every task has a reference, status, assignee, estimate and optional due date.

blocks.heading: Projects and views
blocks.text: List, Board, Timeline and Workload views share the same task data. Timeline shows dependencies and milestones. Workload groups open task estimates by assignee and week so you can spot overallocation.

blocks.heading: Task fields
blocks.text: Task fields include title, description, assignee, reporter, status, priority, estimate, start date, due date, labels, custom fields and attachments. Estimates use person-days and accept increments of 0.5.

blocks.heading: Status and workflow
blocks.text: The default workflow is Backlog, To do, In progress, In review, Blocked and Done. Admins can rename, reorder and add statuses, and choose which statuses count as closed. A task can move backwards if the workflow allows it.

blocks.heading: Comments and mentions
blocks.text: Comments support @mentions, reactions, file attachments and threaded replies. Editing a comment keeps the previous version in the task activity log for 90 days. Resolving a thread hides it from the default comment view.

blocks.heading: Milestones and workload
blocks.text: Add a milestone from the project sidebar and set a target date. Workload view counts open task estimates per assignee. A person is overallocated when assigned estimates exceed their weekly capacity, which defaults to five person-days.

blocks.heading: Saved views and export
blocks.text: Saved views can be personal, shared with a project or published to the workspace. A view stores filters, sort order, grouping, visible columns and the selected layout. CSV exports include visible rows and columns.

blocks.heading: Automations
blocks.text: Project automations can assign a task, change status or post a comment when a trigger fires. Triggers include task created, status changed and due date approaching. Automations run as the workspace owner and appear in the audit log.

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: API keys authenticate server-to-server requests to the Helios API. Send the key in the Authorization header as a Bearer token. Keys are workspace credentials; never ship them in browser code or mobile apps.

blocks.heading: Create a key
blocks.text: Open Settings > Developer > API keys and choose Create key. The full key is shown once. Copy it before closing the dialog; Helios stores only a fingerprint and cannot show the secret again. Keys inherit the permissions of the member who created them.

blocks.heading: Key lifetime
blocks.text: API keys do not expire. Helios does not provide key rotation in v1. To replace a key, create a second key, deploy it, and then revoke the first key. A workspace can have up to ten active keys.

blocks.heading: Rotate a key
blocks.text: Helios does not provide a rotation action in v1. Create a second key, deploy it, verify traffic, and then revoke the first key. A workspace can have up to ten active keys.

blocks.heading: Scopes
blocks.text: Keys have workspace-wide access in v1. There are no read-only or project-scoped keys. Create a separate key per service so that one credential can be revoked without interrupting other integrations.

blocks.heading: Revoke a key
blocks.text: Key creation and revocation appear in Settings > Audit log. Requests made with a key are attributed to the key owner in project activity.

blocks.heading: Common errors
blocks.text: 401 invalid_key means the key is unknown or malformed. 401 key_expired means the key passed its 90-day limit. 403 insufficient_scope means the key is valid but lacks the scope required by the endpoint. Include the request ID from the response when contacting support.

blocks.text: API keys authenticate server-to-server requests to the Helios API. Send the key in the Authorization header as a Bearer token. Keys are workspace credentials; never ship them in browser code or mobile apps.

blocks.heading: Create a key
blocks.text: Open Settings > Developer > API keys and choose Create key. Choose the read, write or admin scope, name the key and copy the secret from the confirmation dialog. The full key is shown once; Helios stores only a fingerprint.

blocks.heading: Key lifetime
blocks.text: API keys expire 90 days after creation. The API returns HTTP 401 with the error code key_expired for an expired key. Rotate keys before day 90; in v2 the old key stops working as soon as rotation completes.

blocks.heading: Rotate a key
blocks.text: Open Settings > Developer > API keys, select a key and choose Rotate. The replacement key is shown once and keeps the same scopes. Update the service environment variable before the old key is revoked; the old key stops working when rotation completes.

blocks.heading: Scopes
blocks.text: Choose scopes when creating a key: read, write or admin. Read keys can list projects and tasks; write keys can create and update them; admin keys can also manage members and webhooks. Grant the smallest scope that the integration needs.

blocks.heading: Revoke a key
blocks.text: Key creation, rotation and revocation emit audit events with the actor, key prefix and source IP address. Request logs retain the key prefix, never the secret.

blocks.heading: Common errors
blocks.text: 401 invalid_key means the key is unknown or malformed. 401 key_expired means the key passed its 90-day limit. 403 insufficient_scope means the key is valid but lacks the scope required by the endpoint. Include the request ID from the response when contacting support.

blocks.text: API keys authenticate server-to-server requests to the Helios API. Send the key in the Authorization header as a Bearer token. Keys are workspace credentials; never ship them in browser code or mobile apps.

blocks.heading: Create a key
blocks.text: Open Settings > Developer > API keys and choose Create key. Choose the read, write or admin scope, optionally limit the key to specific projects on a Business plan, name the key and copy the secret from the confirmation dialog. The full key is shown once.

blocks.heading: Key lifetime
blocks.text: API keys expire 90 days after creation. Rotation creates a 24-hour overlap: the replacement key works immediately and the old key keeps working until the overlap ends. After 24 hours the old key returns HTTP 401 with the error code key_expired.

blocks.heading: Rotate a key
blocks.text: Open Settings > Developer > API keys, select a key and choose Rotate. Choose the overlap window (1 to 24 hours, default 24) and copy the new key. The replacement inherits the original scopes unless you edit them before confirming.

blocks.heading: Scopes
blocks.text: Choose scopes when creating a key: read, write, admin or a comma-separated combination such as read,write. Admin keys can manage members, webhooks and billing exports. Project-scoped keys are available on Business plans and restrict access to listed projects.

blocks.heading: Revoke a key
blocks.text: Key creation, rotation, scope changes and revocation emit audit events with the actor, key prefix and source IP address. The audit log retains key events for 365 days. Request logs retain the key prefix, never the secret.

blocks.heading: Common errors

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: Helios has four built-in roles. Owners manage billing, security and the workspace. Admins manage members, projects and integrations. Members create and edit work. Viewers can read projects but cannot change tasks or settings.

blocks.heading: Assign a role
blocks.text: Open Settings > Members, choose a member and select Change role. Every workspace must keep at least one Owner. A member can hold only one built-in role at a time; custom roles are not available in v1.

blocks.heading: Permissions
blocks.text: Only Owners can change the billing plan, delete the workspace or enable SAML. Admins can invite members, create projects and manage webhooks. Members cannot change workspace settings. Viewers cannot comment on tasks or upload attachments.

blocks.heading: Audit log access
blocks.text: The audit log records member invitations, role changes and project deletions. Owners can view the log under Settings > Audit log. Export is not available in v1.

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: Helios has four built-in roles and optional custom roles. Owners manage billing, security and the workspace. Admins manage members, projects and integrations. Members create and edit work. Viewers and Guests have read-only access with different visibility rules.

blocks.heading: Assign a role
blocks.text: Open Settings > Members, choose a member and select Change role. Every workspace must keep at least one Owner. Guests are invited from a project rather than the workspace directory and only see projects they are added to.

blocks.heading: Permissions
blocks.text: Custom roles start from a built-in role and add granular permissions such as project.create, member.invite and audit.export. A custom role cannot grant billing.manage or workspace.delete; those stay with the Owner role. Permission changes apply at the next request.

blocks.heading: Audit log access
blocks.text: Audit log export requires the Owner role or a custom role with the audit.export permission. The export covers the previous 30 days, is delivered as a CSV download, and the download link expires after seven days. Invitations, role changes, project deletions and SSO changes are always recorded.

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: Helios has four built-in roles, optional custom roles and SCIM group mapping. Owners manage billing, security and the workspace. Admins manage members, projects and integrations. Members create and edit work. Viewers and Guests have read-only access with different visibility rules.

blocks.heading: Assign a role
blocks.text: Open Settings > Members, choose a member and select Change role. Every workspace must keep at least one Owner. Guests are invited from a project and only see projects they are added to. With SCIM enabled, group membership can assign built-in roles automatically.

blocks.heading: Permissions
blocks.text: Custom roles start from a built-in role and add granular permissions such as project.create, member.invite, audit.export and webhook.manage. A custom role cannot grant billing.manage or workspace.delete; those stay with the Owner role. Permission changes apply at the next request.

blocks.heading: Audit log access
blocks.text: Audit log export requires the Owner role or a custom role with the audit.export permission. The export covers the previous 90 days, is delivered as a CSV download, and the download link expires after 24 hours. SCIM provisioning events include the source identity provider and the mapped group.

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: Helios bills per active member. Starter is free for up to five members, Team is USD 12 per member per month billed annually, and Business is USD 24 per member per month billed annually. Monthly billing costs 20 percent more.

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: Single sign-on lets members authenticate through your identity provider instead of a Helios password. SSO is configured per workspace and can be enforced for every member except the break-glass Owner account.

blocks.heading: Session policy
blocks.text: SAML 2.0 single sign-on is available on the Business plan. Helios supports service-provider-initiated and identity-provider-initiated sign-in. Just-in-time provisioning creates a Member account on first sign-in. SAML sessions expire after 24 hours in v1.

blocks.heading: Provisioning
blocks.text: SCIM provisioning is not supported in v1. Member accounts are created by JIT.

blocks.heading: Configure SAML
blocks.text: In your identity provider, create a SAML application and use the workspace metadata URL from Settings > Security > SSO. Set the ACS URL to https://app.helios.example/saml/acs and the entity ID to the workspace ID shown on the same page.

blocks.heading: Configure SAML
blocks.text: Upload the identity provider metadata XML or enter the SSO URL and signing certificate manually. Helios validates the audience, recipient and signature on every assertion. Clock skew is limited to two minutes.

blocks.heading: Verify domains
blocks.text: Add every email domain that should use SSO and verify it with a DNS TXT record. A domain can belong to only one workspace. Members with an unverified domain continue to sign in with their Helios password unless enforcement is on.

blocks.heading: Enforce SSO
blocks.text: Owners can choose Optional or Required. Required SSO blocks password sign-in for every member whose email domain is verified, except the break-glass Owner. Keep at least two Owners with working SSO access before enabling enforcement.

blocks.heading: Troubleshooting
blocks.text: A signature error usually means the certificate in Helios is stale. An audience mismatch means the entity ID in the identity provider does not match the workspace. After changing certificates, sign out and retry in a private browser window.

blocks.heading: Helios 1.0
blocks.text: Helios 1.0 was released on 2024-01-15. This release introduced workspaces, projects, tasks, List and Timeline views, comments and CSV import. It is the first generally available version of the product.

blocks.heading: Highlights
blocks.text: Projects and tasks with references, statuses, assignees and due dates. Email notifications with an optional daily digest. A workspace member directory with Owner, Admin, Member and Viewer roles.

blocks.heading: Improvements
blocks.text: CSV import now accepts priority and labels. Timeline view remembers the last zoom level. Mention notifications include the comment text instead of only a link.

blocks.heading: Known issues
blocks.text: Timeline drag-and-drop can skip a day when the browser zoom is below 80 percent. CSV import rejects files larger than 10 MB. Viewer accounts can still download attachments if they have the direct link.

blocks.heading: Upgrade notes
blocks.text: No action is required for hosted workspaces. API clients should continue using the v1 endpoints. The legacy /projects.json shape is deprecated but still available until 2024-12-31.

blocks.heading: Helios 2.0
blocks.text: Helios 2.0 was released on 2025-01-15. This release added task dependencies, recurring tasks, guest access, board view and scoped API keys. It also introduced the 2.0 API namespace.

blocks.heading: Highlights
blocks.text: Dependencies with timeline warnings. Recurring tasks for daily, weekly and monthly work. Guests who only see the projects they are added to. API keys with read, write and admin scopes.

blocks.heading: Improvements
blocks.text: Project templates copy sections, checklists and custom fields. Saved views can be shared with a project. Audit events now include the source IP address for key changes.

blocks.heading: Breaking changes
blocks.text: API keys created before 2025-01-15 had no scopes and now behave as admin keys. The legacy Slack command /helios has been replaced by the Slack app. Webhook signatures use SHA-256; SHA-1 signatures are still accepted until 2025-06-30.

blocks.heading: Known issues
blocks.text: The CSV importer does not preserve dependency links. Workload view is not available in 2.0. A recurring task may create two occurrences if the browser retries a failed completion request.

blocks.heading: Helios 3.0
blocks.text: Helios 3.0 was released on 2026-01-15. This release added milestones, workload planning, the command palette, SCIM provisioning and 90-day audit log exports. It also made webhook signature verification mandatory.

blocks.heading: Highlights
blocks.text: Milestones with timeline markers. Workload view for capacity planning. Command palette for navigation and common actions. SAML session policy reduced to 8 hours and SCIM group-to-role mapping.

blocks.heading: Improvements
blocks.text: Project automations can assign tasks, change status and post comments. API key rotation supports a 24-hour overlap. Audit exports now cover 90 days and expire after 24 hours. CSV import preserves dependency references by task reference.

blocks.heading: Breaking changes
blocks.text: Webhook requests without a valid SHA-256 signature are rejected. The v1 API is read-only and returns 410 for write requests. Legacy workspace API keys without scopes must be rotated before 2026-04-01.

blocks.heading: Known issues
blocks.text: Workload view does not include tasks without estimates. The command palette can lag by one keystroke on very large workspaces. SCIM group changes can take up to 15 minutes to appear in role assignments.

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: Webhooks send an HTTP POST to your endpoint when an event happens in Helios. Create an endpoint under Settings > Developer > Webhooks, choose the events and store the signing secret securely.

blocks.heading: Signature verification
blocks.text: Each delivery includes an X-Helios-Signature header containing an HMAC-SHA1 digest of the raw request body. Compute the digest with the endpoint secret and compare it in constant time before parsing JSON.

blocks.heading: Retries and delivery
blocks.text: Helios retries failed deliveries three times with a five-minute backoff. A delivery is successful when the endpoint returns any 2xx status within ten seconds. After the final retry the delivery is marked failed and is not retried again.

blocks.heading: Event types
blocks.text: Available events are project.created, project.deleted, task.created, task.updated and task.deleted. Payloads include the workspace ID, event type, timestamp and the changed object.

blocks.heading: Manage endpoints
blocks.text: Rotate a secret from the endpoint menu; the previous secret remains valid for 24 hours. Disable an endpoint to stop new deliveries without deleting its history. Delivery logs retain request headers, response status and latency for 30 days.

blocks.heading: Replay a delivery
blocks.text: Open the endpoint delivery log, select a failed delivery and choose Replay. Replays use the current endpoint secret and count toward the retry budget. A delivery can be replayed up to ten times in 24 hours.

blocks.text: Helios 1.0 supports Slack, GitHub and Google Calendar. Install an integration from Settings > Integrations and authorize the workspace. Each integration has its own permissions page.

blocks.heading: Slack and Teams
blocks.text: The Slack integration posts task and project updates to a channel and lets members create tasks with the /helios slash command. Link a channel to a project to keep updates in one place.

blocks.heading: GitHub and GitLab
blocks.text: The GitHub integration links pull requests and commits to tasks when the task reference appears in the title or body. Merging a linked pull request can move the task to Done if the project enables it.

blocks.heading: Calendar and Jira
blocks.text: The Google Calendar integration mirrors task due dates into a read-only Helios calendar. The Jira integration links Helios tasks to Jira issues and syncs status in both directions when the mapping is enabled.

blocks.heading: Permissions and limits
blocks.text: An integration acts as the member who installed it. If that member leaves the workspace, an Owner must reconnect the integration. Each workspace can have up to 20 active integrations and 100 linked projects.

blocks.heading: Troubleshooting
blocks.text: If an integration stops posting, check Settings > Integrations for an expired authorization and reconnect it. Slack rate limits can delay messages during busy periods. GitHub events are delivered once; Helios does not replay missed events.

blocks.heading: Scope
blocks.text: This policy covers hosted Helios workspaces. It does not cover data that a customer exports and stores outside Helios. Retention periods are measured from the deletion event in UTC.

blocks.heading: Retention schedule
blocks.text: Deleted projects enter a recoverable state for 30 days and are then purged within seven days. Deleted tasks are purged with their project. Audit logs are retained for 180 days. API request logs are retained for 30 days.

blocks.heading: Retention schedule
blocks.text: Backups are encrypted at rest and retained for 35 days. A backup may contain data that was deleted after the backup was taken; restores are performed only for workspace-level recovery.

blocks.heading: Export before deletion
blocks.text: An Owner can export a project before the recoverable period ends. Exports include tasks, comments, attachments and custom fields. The download link expires after 24 hours and is not included in backups.

blocks.heading: Legal hold
blocks.text: A legal hold suspends deletion for named projects or members until an Owner removes the hold. Legal hold is available on Business plans. Helios notifies the workspace owner before a held project is purged.

blocks.heading: On-premises installation retired
blocks.text: Helios ended sales of the on-premises distribution on 2024-12-31. The final supported on-premises release was 1.8. Helios 2.0 and later are cloud-only, and no installer, license key, activation code or upgrade package is available.

blocks.heading: On-premises installation retired
blocks.text: This page is retained so that old bookmarks and support articles do not return a 404. It does not describe a supported installation procedure for Helios 2.0 or 3.0.

blocks.heading: Why the distribution was retired
blocks.text: Operating a self-hosted deployment required customers to manage PostgreSQL, object storage, search indexes and quarterly security patches. The hosted service now provides the same data residency controls in the US and EU regions.

blocks.heading: Migration to the hosted service
blocks.text: An owner of a 1.x deployment can request a migration assessment from Helios Support. The assessment covers data export, identity provider mapping and a cutover window. Migrations are scheduled by support; there is no self-service migration command.

blocks.heading: Migration to the hosted service
blocks.text: Export the PostgreSQL database and attachment bucket before the assessment. Do not send production credentials by email. Support provides a secure upload link after the request is approved.

blocks.heading: Support boundaries
blocks.text: Support cannot issue installation media, patch an existing 1.x server or provide commands from the retired installer. Security advisories for 1.8 are no longer published. Customers still running 1.x should plan a migration or isolate the server from the public internet.

blocks.text: At contract termination Acme receives a full export within ten business days. Acme-specific retention commitment: Helios deletes the workspace 45 days after the termination date, after the export is confirmed. Backups containing Acme data expire within 35 days after deletion.
